description.narrative: In 2022, Europe has been among the fastest “heat wave hot spots” in the world. Many parts of western Europe are experiencing high temperatures, strong winds, low relative humidity and drought conditions causing raging wildfires, impacting thousands of people. According to the European Forest Fire Information System, the weekly cumulative of burnt areas (hectares) in 2022 has already surpassed the averages recorded from 2006-2021. Counties impacted include Greece, Portugal, Spain, France, Italy, Slovenia, Germany, Czech Republic, Croatia, Albania and North Macedonia. On 11 July, The French Prime Minister Antonio Costa was quoted as saying upcoming "conditions of maximum risk" were to be expected. On 14 July, all mainland Portugal was on Red Alert as temperatures reached as high as 45°C. The biggest wildfire in the history of Slovenia was recorded on 15 July. The Red Cross and Red Crescent National Societies have been responding with activities consisting of evacuation support, first aid, the distribution of food, water and psychosocial assistance, among others. National Societies have reported that thousands of people have been affected and displaced, with the latest reports of injuries and deaths in Greece and Portugal. The Emergencies Team monitored the situation from June-August 2022.
